introduction: On this Sunday, the Preacher says, Vanity of vanities, all is vanity, asking what we gain from all our toil. In the Gospel, Jesus warns against greed and tells of a rich man who builds bigger barns but dies that very night, not rich toward God. Paul urges us to set our minds on things above, where Christ is. Let us seek the treasure that lasts.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord teaches us to number our days, that we may gain wisdom of heart. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may witness to a life that is rich toward God, not in possessions. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are consumed by work or worry about money: that they may find rest in God. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the poor and all who lack what they need: that those who have much may share generously. Let us pray to the Lord.
For families divided over inheritance or money: that they may be reconciled. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may set our minds on the things that are above. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, all our possessions pass away, but your love endures forever. Free us from greed, and make us rich in what matters to you. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Rich toward God
reflection.body:
The first reading opens with famous words: "Vanity of vanities, all is vanity." The word vanity here means vapor or breath, something that passes quickly and cannot be held. The Preacher looks at a person who works hard with wisdom and skill, only to leave everything to someone who never worked for it. He asks: "For what does a man have of all his labor and of the striving of his heart?"

In the Gospel, a man asks Jesus to settle an inheritance dispute with his brother. Jesus refuses to be a judge in the matter, but he speaks to the deeper problem: "Beware! Keep yourselves from covetousness, for a man's life doesn't consist of the abundance of the things which he possesses."

Then he tells a parable. A rich man has a great harvest and no room to store it. He decides to pull down his barns and build bigger ones, and then relax: eat, drink and be merry. He talks only to himself and plans only for himself. But God says to him, "You foolish one, tonight your soul is required of you." And God asks a question: "The things which you have prepared", whose will they be?

The man's mistake was not having a good harvest, or planning ahead. It was living as if his possessions were his life, and as if God and others did not exist. Jesus concludes: "So is he who lays up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God."

Paul shows another way: "Set your mind on the things that are above, not on the things that are on the earth." He adds that greed "is idolatry," because it makes possessions into a god.

The psalm prays, "So teach us to count our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom." This week, look at what you are storing up. Give something away generously. And ask what it means for you to be rich toward God.
